title: Desktop item intent v2
description: desktopItemsHost request (the root) plus, under $defs, the desktop-items-quantity-1 quantity-buy reply result, refusal details and ledger entry. HolobotsMobile desktop-items-quantity-1 (HolobotsUnity DECISIONS #72.32; mirrors market-quantity-host-1 / Mobile #175 for the healing items). The root is HolobotsUnity Schemas/desktop-items-v2.schema.json with one additive optional field, `quantity`; schemaVersion stays desktop-items-2 (the currentHealth precedent). Host-authoritative (hard rule 1): the host prices, spends, grants and refuses; clients send the request and present the reply. A 'buy' carrying `quantity` (integer 1-99) buys that many of ONE healing item (item.emergency_patch, item.repair_kit, item.full_restore) as ONE purchase: Holos spent = unit price x quantity in the same users/{uid} update that raises the stock by quantity; one onboarding market beat; one server-only ledger entry per requestId, the existing receipt itemInventories/{uid}/receipts/{requestId} (#/$defs/receipt; rules deny clients; account deletion removes it); a retry with the same requestId replays the stored reply with alreadyProcessed true and never buys twice; the same requestId for another item or quantity is sequence_conflict. A healing stock may not pass the cap of 999 after a quantity buy. `quantity` on any other operation or item, or beside packId / holobotId / currentHealth, is invalid_request. A request without `quantity` is the legacy one-per-buy request: reply, refusals, receipt identity and writes unchanged byte for byte. Refusals are callable errors (failed-precondition, message = the code) whose details are #/$defs/quantityRefusalDetails, checked in this order: invalid_request, unavailable (no profile), replay or sequence_conflict, between_battles_only (an open zone expedition), unavailable (malformed balance or stock, never coerced), over_cap (details cap/owned/maxQuantity), not_enough_holos (details price/holosTokens/shortfall). A refusal writes nothing. Clients key on details.rejectionCode.

currentHealth.description: healing-items-2 (HolobotsMobile 147cfb5 desktopItemsHost): optional presented-HP observation on a 'use' with holobotId inside an open zone run (or a duel-healing-1 run). Never above the host-issued vitals or the ledger; the host refuses higher (invalid_request) and heals from it.

quantity.description: desktop-items-quantity-1 (HolobotsMobile desktopItemsHost, DECISIONS #72.32): optional on a 'buy' of a healing item only: how many units ONE purchase buys. (Not the vendor-3 listing's own `quantity`, which is the units one listing purchase grants: 1 for each healing item.) Absent = the legacy one-per-buy request. The host refuses it anywhere else (invalid_request).

healingItemId.description: The items a quantity buy may name (lib/repairItems.ts HEALING_ITEMS).

quantityBuyResult.description: `result` of a quantity buy's reply. A legacy buy keeps {kind: 'buy', itemId}.

unitPrice.description: Holos for one unit (the vendor-3 listing price).

owned.description: The stock after the purchase (also the item row's owned in the same reply).

quantityBuyReply.description: A quantity buy's reply: the desktop-items-2 inventory snapshot after the purchase (every other field unchanged from today's reply) with result = #/$defs/quantityBuyResult. alreadyProcessed is present (true) only on a replay, as for every desktopItemsHost receipt.

quantityRefusalDetails.description: details of a quantity-buy callable error (HttpsError failed-precondition, message = the code). over_cap and not_enough_holos carry the host's numbers for the max / shortfall line.

maxQuantity.description: The most this pilot can buy now before the cap: cap - owned, floored at 0.

price.description: Holos the purchase would spend: unitPrice x quantity.

receipt.description: The one ledger entry per requestId: itemInventories/{uid}/receipts/{requestId} (the existing desktopItemsHost receipt; a quantity buy adds nothing new). identity is the validated request as JSON, so it includes quantity. Server-only (Firestore rules deny clients); documented for host tests and audits.
